THE STARTING POINT

What you can build from here.

A good starting point when…

Developers who already think in relational tables and want to explore conversational access to PostgreSQL.

  • Hybrid retrieval using pgvector and PostgreSQL full-text search.
  • Optional function calling to translate questions into query filters.
  • React frontend and Python FastAPI backend.
  • Managed-identity access to Azure resources.
Before choosing this template

Runtime requirements are summarized from the README; model quota, region support and costs still need checking. No deployment was performed.

BEFORE YOU START

Check your environment.

  • Azure Developer CLI, Git, Node.js 18+ and Python 3.10+.
  • PostgreSQL 14+, pgvector and Docker Desktop for the local setup described in the README.
  • Azure subscription and adequate model quota; verify model availability in your target regions.

For every deployment: confirm your subscription, permissions, target region, model quota where applicable, and likely charges. Reading this page does not validate any of those.

FROM EVALUATION TO ACTION

Your next steps, in order.

  1. Review the template and its hooks.

    Inspect repository setup scripts, required permissions and deployment instructions before executing code.

  2. Initialize a new project.

    Use a new directory, then run the template's init command.

    azd init -t rag-postgres-openai-python
    Repository setup instructions ↗

  3. Review costs, then approve deployment.

    Follow the repository guide to authenticate, configure your environment and deploy. Cloud resources can incur charges even after an interrupted deployment. Nothing on this website runs azd up for you.

    Open the Azure pricing calculator ↗

  4. Clean up when you are finished.

    azd down deletes the resources created for an environment. Review the target environment and approve deletion before running it.
